blocks.x: How Cyber & Zero-Trust lands in Capital Markets & Wealth Management — the constraints that shape the build, the gated delivery pattern, and the deltas we commit against your baseline.

Wealth and capital-markets clients buy judgment and pay for experience: advisors need research and portfolio context in minutes, operations need settlement and reconciliation without firefights, and compliance needs evidence without expeditions.

items: HNW records concentrate spear-phishing and exfiltration value; controls are generic, not tiered by risk.
Advisors assemble portfolio context from terminals, PDFs and CRM; response quality depends on prep time.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Identity & Access Modernization, Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation, Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Advisor research and prep, Reconciliation and breaks, Client reporting) on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — MiFID II / fiduciary regimes among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Evidence once, audit anywhere: compliance automation across SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, DORA and privacy.
Never trust, always verify: zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Detection that keeps pace: intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
Risk-tiered controls for HNW data with monitoring (exfiltration paths closed)

blocks.caption: Regimes shaping this capability
rows: ICT risk, incident reporting, resilience testing and third-party oversight obligations with supervisory scrutiny

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Banking & Financial Services level this capability reads as: identity-centric access, microsegmentation and workload identity across branch, office and datacenter zones (lateral-movement paths eliminated in purple-team validation). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Delivery runs on one weekly rhythm for every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
